You're correct. That would have been drift.
The mission is still:

Finish Runtime Operations first.

Runtime Operations is the production reference implementation.

Only after Runtime Operations is complete do we extract common patterns into the Lumina design system.

The metric cards we were discussing are Runtime metric cards, not LuminaMetricCard as a design-system component.
That means the next work belongs in:
apps/lumina-builder/src/components/workspaces/runtime/parts/RuntimeHeader.tsx
—not in:
apps/lumina-builder/src/components/lumina/workspace/LuminaMetricCard.tsx
The objective is to make the Runtime hero metrics look first-class by refining how they are composed and presented, while leaving the shared component alone until the Runtime workspace has been fully validated.
The refinement should focus on the Runtime-specific presentation:


Premium composition of each metric.


Better hierarchy between primary and secondary values.


Runtime-specific operational accents.


More polished icon treatments.


Better semantic visual language.


Richer footer content.


Better alignment between the four cards.


Stronger visual relationship with the Runtime hero.


Only after Runtime Operations reaches production quality do we evaluate what should be generalized into LuminaMetricCard and the broader Lumina design system.
That's the correct sequence, and I'll keep following it.
Draft a handoff for the next conversation to continue the workflow without breaking it, with no drift. Premium grade, premium production grade, first in class.

Do not redesign the architecture.
Do not extract reusable components.
Do not refactor shared components.
The Runtime Operations workspace is the reference implementation. Only after it is completely polished and production-ready should patterns be extracted into the Lumina design system.

Also add that they have to commit and push so we don't lose any work.

Yes. Since this is a long-running reconstruction effort, every completed milestone should be preserved immediately. I would add the following section to the handoff.

Source Control Policy (Mandatory)
Every completed refinement must be preserved before proceeding to the next task.
Never accumulate multiple completed milestones without committing them.
The workflow is:


Implement one focused refinement.


Verify the application builds successfully.


Validate the UI manually.


Commit the completed work.


Push the branch to the remote repository.


Continue with the next refinement.


This ensures that no production-quality work is lost and every milestone has a recoverable checkpoint.

Required Validation
Before every commit:
Bashnpm run build
The build must be green.
Do not commit failing builds.

Commit Policy
Each commit should represent one logical refinement.
Avoid combining unrelated visual improvements into a single commit.
Examples:


refactor(runtime): refine runtime hero metrics


feat(runtime): polish runtime project cards


style(runtime): improve runtime inspector hierarchy


refactor(runtime): refine event stream presentation


Commits should be small, reviewable, and easy to revert independently.

Push Policy
After every successful commit:
Bashgit push
Do not leave completed work only in the local repository.
The remote branch is the recovery point for the project.

Recovery Rule
At the completion of every production-quality milestone:


Build passes.


Manual validation passes.


Commit created.


Push completed.


Only then may work continue to the next Runtime Operations refinement.
This policy is mandatory throughout the Runtime Operations premium polish and continues until the workspace reaches production-ready status. It minimizes the risk of losing work and provides a clean history of each completed refinement.
